Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate the above parabola. Express your answer in the form $x=2pt,y=p{t}^{2},$ where $p$ is a constant.

$x=$
{{field-1}},
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(1,2).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(1,2),$ we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=2$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}1=2pt \\ 2=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =2pt \\ \frac{1}{2} & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =p{(\frac{1}{2p})}^{2} \\ 2 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{4{p}^{2}} \\ 2 & =\frac{1}{4p} \\ p & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(\frac{1}{8})t,\,y=(\frac{1}{8}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=\frac{1}{4}t,\,y=\frac{1}{8}{t}^{2}.
$$
